consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning: 'meat' (solid food) symbolizes advanced/mature spiritual teaching or deeper doctrine, explicitly contrasted with 'milk' as elementary instruction for spiritual infants (1 Cor 3:1–2; Heb 5:12–14).
book_summary: Book: meat is the word obeyed to completeness; milk is the word received, and meat is that same word carried through to full obedience with senses exercised to discern.
consensus_core_identification: Advanced/mature spiritual teaching (deeper doctrine content) for the spiritually grown, versus milk as elementary teaching.
book_core_identification: The same word carried through to complete obedience (reception completed in doing), with exercised discernment.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus bounds meat by depth/maturity of teaching content distinct from milk; the book bounds meat by degree of obedience to the same word (received vs fully obeyed), not by advanced versus elementary doctrine.
material_contradiction: Consensus treats meat and milk as different levels of doctrinal content; the book treats them as the same word at different stages (reception vs complete obedience), so the central milk/meat identification cannot both hold in the same sense.
rationale: Minimum cores conflict: settled consensus centers meat on mature doctrine (1 Cor 3; Heb 5), while the book replaces that referent with complete obedience of the word, aligning more with John 4:34-type will-doing and re-reading Heb 5:14 around exercised senses rather than advanced teaching content. Shared passages do not make the cores equivalent; accepting the book requires rejecting the consensus primary identification.
strongest_objection: 1 Corinthians 3:1–2 and Hebrews 5:12–14 present meat/solid food as teaching the immature cannot yet bear—i.e., advanced content—not merely elementary word fully obeyed.
